transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time not thinking about how I look. It sounds kind of silly saying it out loud, but at work, under the restaurant lights, I keep feeling like my hairline and my face make me look… old, or strange. My coworkers say they don’t see it, so maybe I’m making too much of it, but I can’t seem to stop thinking about it.
How much distress do these thoughts about your appearance cause you?

It’s… honestly pretty upsetting. I try to tell myself it’s not a big deal, and I know other people say they don’t see it, but I can’t stop thinking that my hairline and my face under those restaurant lights make me look old or strange. It gets to me more than I’d like to admit.
Do you find yourself worrying about your appearance in other situations besides under the restaurant lights at work?

Mostly it’s under the restaurant lights at work, I think. That’s where it really grabs me — my hairline, and just the way my face looks, like I look old or kind of strange. I know my coworkers say they don’t see what I’m talking about, so I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is… but it’s hard for me to stop thinking about it.
Does this concern about your appearance bother you when you're alone, or is it mainly when you're around other people or at work?

It’s mainly at work, when I’m around people and those lights are on me. I mean… I do think about it outside of that too, but the restaurant is where it feels the worst. I keep getting stuck on my hairline and how my face looks there, like I look old or strange, even though my coworkers tell me they don’t see it. I know that probably sounds a little excessive.
Is it always your hairline and face that you're concerned about, or are there other parts of your body that you worry about as well?

It’s mostly the hairline and my face, yeah. I don’t really… I mean, I’m not here because of other body parts or anything like that. It’s that when I’m under the restaurant lights, I can’t stop thinking I look old or strange, even though people at work tell me they don’t see it. I know that probably sounds kind of silly, but that’s the thing I keep getting stuck on.
Do you think your concerns about your hairline and face are realistic?

I mean… I want to say maybe I’m overreacting a little, because my coworkers keep telling me they don’t see what I’m talking about. But to me, under those restaurant lights, it really does look like my hairline and my face make me look old or strange. I can’t seem to stop thinking about it, even though I know other people don’t seem to notice it.
Is your concern about your hairline and face affecting your ability to do your job or interact with others outside of work?

Yeah… I mean, I wish I could say it wasn’t, but it has. At work I’ve been late or missed shifts because I just couldn’t get myself together to be seen like that, and I’ve been written up for it. I know that’s not great.

And outside of work, I’ve kind of stopped doing certain things… like staff photos, gallery events, hikes with people. I tell myself I’m just busy or not in the mood, but really it’s because I don’t want to be looked at that way. Does that make sense?
Do you think other people can see that your hairline and face make you look old or strange when you're under the restaurant lights?

I… I think they can, yes. Or at least, that’s how it feels to me under those lights. My hairline and my face just look older and kind of strange, and I get really stuck on it.

But then my coworkers tell me they don’t see what I’m talking about, so… I don’t know. I know maybe I’m making too much of it, but it’s hard for me to believe they can’t see it at all. Does that make sense?
Do you think you would still be concerned about your appearance if your hairline and face looked different under the restaurant lights?

I think… yes, probably. I mean, maybe the lights make it worse, or at least that’s what I tell myself, but it’s not only the lights. I’m here because I just can’t stop thinking about my hairline and how my face looks—like it makes me look old or strange.

Even when people at work say they don’t see it, I still get stuck on it. I know that might sound excessive, but that’s honestly what’s been happening.
Is your concern about your appearance focused on this one issue with your hairline and face, or do you think there could be other flaws that you're not noticing yet?

I think it’s mostly this… my hairline and my face, especially under the restaurant lights. That’s the thing I can’t seem to let go of.

I don’t know if there are other flaws I’m not noticing yet—I hope not. I guess I’m already pretty stuck on feeling like my hairline and the way my face looks make me look old or strange, even when people at work tell me they don’t see it. I know that probably sounds like too much, but that’s what keeps coming up for me.
Do you think your perception of your hairline and face is the same as how others see you?

Not exactly, no… I mean, I want to say maybe they’re just being polite, but my coworkers keep telling me they don’t see what I’m talking about.

So I guess my perception probably isn’t the same as theirs. It’s just… I can’t stop seeing my hairline and my face under those restaurant lights as making me look old and strange. I know that may sound like I’m overdoing it, but that’s why I’m here.
Do you find it difficult to push these thoughts about your hairline and face out of your mind once they start?

Yes… it is difficult. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but once I start thinking about my hairline or how my face looks under those restaurant lights, it just kind of stays there.

Even if my coworkers say they don’t see what I’m talking about, I keep coming back to it—like I look old or strange. I know that probably sounds like too much, but I really can’t seem to stop thinking about it.
Would you say that these thoughts about your hairline and face come into your mind against your will?

Yes… I think so. I don’t really choose to think about it. It just comes in, especially when I’m at work under those restaurant lights, and then I’m stuck on my hairline and my face looking old or strange.

I know my coworkers say they don’t see what I’m talking about, so maybe I’m making too much of it… but it still keeps coming into my mind anyway.
Do you feel like you're trying to avoid thinking about your hairline and face, but the thoughts keep coming back anyway?

Yes… I do try not to think about it. I’ll tell myself, “Just focus on work, people don’t see it,” especially because my coworkers keep saying they don’t notice what I’m talking about.

But then the lights hit a certain way, or I catch myself thinking about my hairline or my face, and it comes right back. I know it may sound like I’m making too much of it, but that’s really why I’m here—I can’t seem to stop thinking that I look old and strange.
Do you feel like these thoughts about your appearance are invading your mind without you wanting them to?

Yes… that’s a fair way to put it, I think. I don’t want to overstate it, but it feels like it gets into my mind whether I want it there or not.

That’s really why I’m here—I can’t stop thinking that my hairline and the way my face looks under the restaurant lights make me look old and strange. And even when my coworkers tell me they don’t see what I’m talking about, I still keep going back to it.
Do you feel like these thoughts about your hairline and face are unwanted and are interrupting your other thoughts?

Yes… I think that’s right. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but it does feel unwanted, and it kind of cuts into whatever else I’m trying to focus on.

I’m here because I just can’t stop thinking that my hairline and the way my face looks under those restaurant lights make me look old and strange. Even when my coworkers tell me they don’t see it, I still keep getting pulled back to it.
Do you feel like these thoughts about your appearance are in line with how you see yourself as a person?

I’m not sure I totally understand what you mean by “in line with how I see myself.” I mean… I don’t think of myself as someone who’s vain or obsessed with looks, if that’s what you mean.

So in that sense, no, it doesn’t really feel like me. It feels embarrassing, honestly. But at the same time, when I see it, it feels very real to me. Does that make sense?
Have these thoughts about your hairline and face affected your relationships with friends or family outside of work?

Yeah… I guess it has, more than I’d like to admit.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just avoiding everyone, but I’ve stopped going to things I used to say yes to—staff photos, gallery events, hikes with people—because I just can’t handle being seen that way. It feels embarrassing to even say that.

And, um… it’s affected work too. I’ve been written up at the restaurant because I’ve been late or missed shifts. I know that’s not exactly friends or family, but it’s part of the same thing, I think. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like these thoughts about your hairline and face are forcing themselves into your mind?

Yeah… I think “forcing themselves in” is probably fair. I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s like I’ll be trying to do something normal, and then the thought about my hairline or my face under the restaurant lights just kind of barges in.

Even if someone at work says they don’t see what I’m talking about, I still can’t seem to let it go. I keep coming back to this idea that I look old or strange. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel like these thoughts about your appearance are popping into your mind without any trigger or warning?

Yeah… I think sometimes it does come up out of nowhere. Or it feels that way.

Like, I’ll be doing something else, and suddenly I’m thinking about my hairline or how my face must look under those restaurant lights—like I look old or strange. I know my coworkers say they don’t really see it, so I feel kind of silly saying it, but I can’t seem to stop thinking about it once it’s there.

Is that what you mean by without a trigger?
